title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp: additive Cheon v3 (one addition per BSGS step, complete hash accounting, floor-rounded success)

claims.statement: For the protected BLS12-381 G1 target with auxiliary powers and every n with 2^20 <= n < r, the deterministic algorithm in proof.md recovers s with heuristic success probability at least 0.401 (at least 0.39; the model value 1 - e^-0.52 = 0.40548 floor-rounded, minus a 0.004 measured-deficit allowance covering every toy-measured coverage deficit) over the uniform challenge. The algorithm is Cheon's p-1 baby-step/giant-step in the subgroup H of 2^20-th powers. Its baby and giant sets are small integers a*b in H (a a prime in (2^75, 2^76], b <= 2^70, chi(a)+chi(b)=0), walked in increasing order at one batched affine G1 addition per element. It uses the 6-element symmetry group {±1, ±λ, ±λ²} via the hash key min(y, p-y). Provenance: the declared dependency cbadde77; every identity, itemisation and bound below is this package's own, restated in proof.md and re-verified by this package's runs. The per-element budgets: canonical y 30 (itemised ~25), walk bookkeeping 100 (itemised ~75), hash insert/lookup 240 (a complete per-transfer accounting: endpoint 61 plus six radix-1024 relay stages of 29 instructions each - 18 word moves, 4 destination selection, 4 queue updates, 3 control - over the sharded table; the linear-probing and sharding model is evidenced by a 65,536-key toy check measuring 1.494/2.468 mean probes against the 1.5/2.5 bounds and shard loads within 2.6 sigma). Its total work W(n) = W(2^20) is at most 2^116.911621 target-group-operation equivalents. This includes the distributed hash-table inserts and lookups, walk bookkeeping, per-prime tables, character precomputation and sieves, collision verification, the d-th root, the final mu_d search and input checks. Preprocessing (challenge-independent work) is at most 2^115.871 and is included. Peak memory is at most 2^122.9 bytes; there is no nonuniform advice. Heuristics: H1 (the product set U*B*G^-1 has random-like coincidences apart from a bounded repeated-rational loss below 10^-4); H2 (characters of the primes a used are equidistributed, affecting only how many primes are needed, with at least 3x slack); and expected-cost hashing and sharding. All are disclosed and supported by toy experiments at their stated scope. This is an analytic bound, not a full-size execution.

experiments.purpose: One run with four parts. (1) Recomputes the v3 cost ledger (canonical y 30, hash 240, bookkeeping 100; every charge asserted above its itemised count) and the exact score. (2) Toy coverage for H1/H2 across X2/d against 1 - exp(-K). (3) A 65,536-key hash_probe check of the linear-probing and sharding model. (4) The full end-to-end toy attack on a 24-bit j = 0 curve with d = 2^6 and GMAX = 16 so the overflow-chunk path executes; every recovered scalar checked. Toy results are evidence at their scale only. Input: K, cov_bits, cov_logd, atk_bits, atk_logd, trials, gmax, seed.
